rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
$$\text{Aufbau: smaller }(n+l)\text{ first; tie} \rightarrow \text{smaller }n$$
$$\text{subshell capacity}=2(2l+1),\qquad \text{shell capacity}=2n^{2}$$
$$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\ \text{BM},\quad n=\text{unpaired electrons}$$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ 4s is always lower in energy than 3d. ✅ It fills first in neutral atoms, but in ions the 4s electrons are removed first (Fe²⁺ = 3d⁶).  ·  ❌ Pauli's principle forbids two electrons in one orbital. ✅ They may share an orbital if their spins are opposite (different mₛ).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Cr (24) = [Ar]3d⁵4s¹ and Cu (29) = [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ are the only anomalies within Z ≤ 30.  ·  Fe³⁺ = [Ar]3d⁵ (5 unpaired); Zn²⁺ = [Ar]3d¹⁰ (0 unpaired).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** Configuration and magnetic behaviour of Cu²⁺. **Solution:** Cu = [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ → Cu²⁺ = [Ar]3d⁹ → one unpaired electron → paramagnetic, μ ≈ 1.73 BM.  ·  **Problem:** How many Zn electrons have l = 2? **Solution:** Zn = [Ar]3d¹⁰4s² — the 3d subshell (l = 2) holds 10 electrons.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Meaning  ·  These three rules distribute electrons among the orbitals of an atom in its ground state: Aufbau fixes the *order* of filling, Pauli fixes the *capacity* of an orbital, and Hund fixes *how degenerate orbitals are filled*.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 2. Aufbau principle and the (n + l) rule  ·  Electrons fill the available orbital of lowest energy first. Order is given by the **Madelung (n + l) rule**: smaller (n + l) first; for equal (n + l), smaller n first. Thus 4s (n + l = 4) fills before 3d (n + l = 5), giving 1s < 2s < 2p < 3s < 3p < 4s < 3d < 4p < 5s < 4d < 5p < 6s < 4f < 5d < 6p < 7s < 5f < 6d < 7p.  ·  ### 3. Pauli's exclusion principle

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: • Ions  ·  • Up to atomic no. 30  ·  ❌ Hund's rule says electrons pair as soon as possible. ✅ Pairing begins only after every degenerate orbital holds one electron.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Cr is [Ar]3d⁴4s². ✅ It is [Ar]3d⁵4s¹ because the half-filled d subshell wins on exchange energy.  ·  State Aufbau's principle, Pauli's exclusion principle and Hund's rule with one example each.  ·  Apply the (n + l) rule to arrange 3d, 4s, 4p, 3p and 5s in order of filling.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: No two electrons in an atom can have all four quantum numbers identical; equivalently an orbital holds at most two electrons with opposite spins (↑↓). Consequences: subshell capacities 2, 6, 10, 14; shell capacity 2n².  ·  ### 4. Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity  ·  Electrons enter degenerate orbitals (same n and l, e.g. the three 2p) singly with parallel spins before pairing; pairing starts only after every degenerate orbital has one electron. Reason: pairing costs Coulomb repulsion energy while parallel spins gain exchange energy.…
